nodes.name: Synthesis league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which fragments of lost memories are scattered through Wraeclast; the player stabilises them and links them in the Memory Nexus. Guide NPC Cavas turns out to be the High Templar Venarius. Not added to the core game; its bosses (Synthetes, Venarius) survive as unique maps.

nodes.name: Blight league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which Sister Cassia asks the exile to defend a Purification Pump against fungal Blight growths; rewards Oils used to Anoint items.

nodes.name: Metamorph league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the alchemist Tane Octavius has the exile gather organs from monsters to build shape-changing Metamorphs; introduces Catalysts.

nodes.name: Delirium league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which Mirrors of Delirium in each area release a spreading fog of madness; leads to the Simulacrum and Cluster Jewels.

nodes.name: Harvest league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the Azmeri outcast Oshabi has the exile plant seeds in the Sacred Grove and harvest Lifeforce for crafting; ends with the Avatar of the Grove boss. Later reworked into a core mechanic.

nodes.name: Heist league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the exile uses Rogue's Markers to enter the Rogue Harbour, run Contracts for the Ring, and hire rogues to steal valuables from fortified caches (Contracts, Blueprints, Grand Heists).

nodes.name: Ritual league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which a Ritual Altar in each zone starts a wave fight that awards Tribute, spendable on a shop of pre-identified items. Narrative content is minimal in PoE1; the same Ritual altar mechanic returns in PoE2's Forbidden Rites league (0.5.5).

nodes.name: Ultimatum league
nodes.summary: Vaal-themed challenge league in which the Trialmaster, servant of the entity Chaos, offers escalating Trials of Chaos for the player to risk or bank rewards. Re-integrated into the core game in 3.23.0.

nodes.name: Expedition league
nodes.summary: Challenge league introducing four Kalguuran expedition NPCs (Gwennen, Tujen, Rog, Dannig) who excavate the lost settlements of their ancestors with explosives. The Kalguur are referenced again in Settlers (Kingsmarch) and in PoE2.

nodes.name: Scourge league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which The Last to Die gives the exile a Blood Crucible to corrupt items while fighting through a demon-ridden 'Nightmare' mirror of Wraeclast; its monsters became the new Beyond monsters.

nodes.name: Archnemesis league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which petrified monsters are imbued with itemised Archnemesis modifiers to build custom rare boss fights. Mechanics-driven; no dedicated narrative NPC in the wiki corpus.

nodes.name: Sentinel league
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which Sentinel drones empower monsters; Power Cores charge Sentinel filaments and Recombinators combine two equipment items. Sentinel mechanics were added to the core game in 3.25; existing Recombinators remained usable.

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra league
aliases: Path of Exile: Lake of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Challenge league in which the player assembles a Mirrored Tablet of reflected encounters and enters the Lake of Kalandra, meeting the ancient trapped entity Kalandra.

chronology.relative: 3.19.0 'Path of Exile: Lake of Kalandra', 2022-08-19 to 2022-12-06

nodes.name: Runes of Aldur league (PoE2)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access temporary league (0.5.0 'Return of the Ancients', 2026-05-29) in which Farrow studies runes on Verisium Remnants; brings Kalguuran runesmithing, Ward and Kalguuran gems to PoE2.

nodes.name: Forbidden Rites league (PoE2)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access event league (0.5.5, 2026-09-04) built on Ritual altars in campaign and endgame zones, with unique-boss Ritual clusters per act and Sacred Bloom Wildwood encounters; 0.5.5 also integrates Runes of Aldur and Expedition into the core PoE2 game.

sources.locator: lead, 'League content' and unique boss rituals

nodes.name: Day Zero rule (league narrative)
nodes.summary: Dev narrative rule: each league story begins with the exile face-down on the Twilight Strand, just exiled by Dominus, so league events cannot build on what the exile did in earlier leagues. Earlier events are attributed to other exiles or remembered as memories.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule; cites 'Integrating League Stories' and ExileCon 2019 dev talks)

nodes.name: Cavas
nodes.summary: Amnesiac 'forgotten spirit' NPC of Synthesis who opens memory zones for the exile; he recovers his memories in the Atlas and is revealed to be High Templar Venarius, thereafter an antagonist while Zana takes over his guide role.

nodes.name: Memory Nexus
nodes.summary: Hub area of Synthesis where captured Fragmented Memories are placed to form paths to rewards, enhancements and boss memories.

nodes.name: Fragmented Memory
nodes.summary: Decaying memory sub-zones found throughout Wraeclast in Synthesis; some are memories of real events (e.g. Malachai's slave mines, gemling experiments, the Templar Laboratory) and are used by the wiki as lore sources.

sources.locator: citations of 'Abandoned Shaft Memory' and 'Eternal Residence Memory'

nodes.name: Memory of the Templar Laboratory
nodes.summary: Tier-5+ Synthesis memory in which Cavas sees High Templar Venarius and the scientist Valdo Caeserius building something together; Venarius lashes out, triggering the realisation of Cavas's identity.

chronology.relative: Past of the Templar Laboratory, shortly before Valdo's imprisonment

nodes.name: Synthetes
nodes.summary: Synthesis league bosses (Altered, Augmented, Rewritten and Twisted Synthete) guarding fractured uniques; later unique-map bosses.

sources.locator: unique items paragraph listing Altered/Augmented/Rewritten/Twisted Synthete

nodes.name: Sister Cassia
nodes.summary: Former Templar-circle mechanical artisan and Blight NPC who runs the Purification Pump encounters and the Anoint bench; exiled by High Templar Dominus for subverting his virtue-gem projects, and replaced by Piety. Believes Blighted maps lead to the Blight's source.

sources.locator: lead; Dialogue: Exile, Replacement, Devices, Fungi, Blighted Maps

nodes.name: Blight (fungal growth)
nodes.summary: Fungal growths infesting Wraeclast whose mycelium spawns monster waves once a Purification Pump pierces it. Cassia first thought it a symptom of Wraeclast's death, then a parasite, and suspects a central growth that Blighted maps lead to.

nodes.name: Purification Pump
nodes.summary: Portable purifying-pumping unit that Sister Cassia places on Blight fungal growths; Blight towers, powered by the fungus's toxic fluid, defend it.

nodes.name: Blightheart
nodes.summary: Hypothesised original source of the Blight. Dhunan (historical Order of the Djinn 'Blightmaster') theorised its existence; Sister Cassia independently suspects a central growth that the Blighted maps lead to. No in-game confirmation is cited.

sources.locator: member list (Dhunan) and Blight Scarabs section

nodes.name: Dhunan
nodes.summary: Historical Order of the Djinn member, 'Blightmaster', a castaway who knew how to contain the Blight and theorised the Blightheart.

nodes.name: Tane Octavius
nodes.summary: Freed slave and alchemist exiled for killing his abusive master Lucan Octavius; works from an underground laboratory (Karui Shores) to isolate 'intrinsic darkness' from the flesh of monsters via Metamorphs, hoping to purify a cruel soul.

sources.locator: lead; Dialogue: Tane's Master, Exile, Vision, Goals

nodes.name: Lucan Octavius
nodes.summary: Wealthy Oriathan alchemist, Tane's master; publicly genial but violent and lustful in private; killed by Tane, who was exiled for it.

nodes.name: Intrinsic darkness
nodes.summary: Tane's term for the cruelty/ill-will in living beings that Metamorphs distil from monster organs; he now thinks it older and more universal than Corruption and hopes to destroy it while leaving the flesh unharmed.

nodes.name: Metamorph
nodes.summary: Shape-shifting enemies assembled from organs of other monsters and bosses; they use the moves of whatever parts they carry.

nodes.name: Tane's Laboratory
nodes.summary: Underground laboratory of Tane Octavius near the Karui Shores, undamaged by Oriath's destruction; where Metamorph work is done.

nodes.name: Saresh, Necromancer of the Weeping Black
nodes.summary: Historical Faridun reject and Order of the Djinn member who explored intrinsic darkness and raised undead until killed by Garukhan; his name is on Metamorph Scarabs.

nodes.name: Delirium
nodes.summary: Fog of madness released through Mirrors of Delirium that spawns and strengthens monsters and can lead to the Simulacrum. Origin is only hinted: Kalandra links it to 'the Trickster' and PoE2 ties Tangmazu to a tutorial Delirium encounter.

nodes.name: Mirror of Delirium
nodes.summary: Mirror found in each area during Delirium league; passing through creates the Delirium fog. Still appears in story maps and league-modifier maps after the league.

nodes.name: The Simulacrum
nodes.summary: The Simulacrum: a wave-based Delirium encounter opened by the Simulacrum map fragment in a Map Device; the fragment is crafted from Simulacrum Splinters dropped by Delirium monsters.

nodes.name: Tangmazu
nodes.summary: Trickster god (Tekaru to the Karui, Black Crow to the Ezomytes), Ralakesh's brother, said to have made Solaris and Lunaris fight; listed on the wiki as an NPC related to Delirium and, in PoE2, revealed as the disguised Freya Hartlin whose release triggers a Delirium encounter.

sources.locator: Quest: Journey's End and Tangmazu reveal
Solaris, Lunaris and Viridi footnote on the Raven Trickster

nodes.name: Oshabi
nodes.summary: Azmeri outcast, exiled by her tribe after she offered a child to the earth when she alone still heard the land's whispers. Tends the Sacred Grove, names the energy Lifeforce and asks the exile to harvest seeds. After the tutorial quest she turns into the Heart of the Grove; she returns as Oshabi, Avatar of the Grove, a boss.

sources.locator: lead; Dialogue: Introduction, The Grove, Lifeforce, Exile from the Azmeri

nodes.name: Oshabi's exile from the Azmeri
nodes.summary: Oshabi, hearing the land demand a sacrifice, offered a child to the earth; her tribe stopped it, the land fell silent, and the Azmeri exiled her and forbade her name.

nodes.name: The Sacred Grove
nodes.summary: Ancient garden carved from the land (possibly by ancestral Azmeri, 'older than the Eternal Empire') where Oshabi plants seeds; restored her connection to the land.

nodes.name: Lifeforce
nodes.summary: Oshabi's name for the invisible force that revives the dead and shapes beasts and plants, released by Grove seeds in Wild, Vivid and Primal forms; she notes its similarity to Corruption and calls them perhaps 'two sides of the same leaf'.

sources.locator: Dialogue: Lifeforce, The Slaying of Malachai, Monsters

nodes.name: Humours / Wisps (Wildwood)
nodes.summary: In the Viridian Wildwood the four humours (Primal, Vivid, Wild, Sacred) materialise as wisps. The first three share names with Harvest's Primal, Vivid and Wild Lifeforce colours. Sacred humours are harvested by the ritual altars of the King in the Mists.

nodes.name: Oshabi, Avatar of the Grove
nodes.summary: Boss form of Oshabi. It is triggered in a Map Device by a Sacred Blossom map fragment; the Heart of the Grove, grown from a harvested Tier 4 seed, is the separate challenge that leads to the Avatar of the Grove.

sources.locator: League mechanic: Heart of the Grove

nodes.name: The Rogue Harbour
nodes.summary: Hub town of the criminal guild known as the Ring, reached by a Rogue's Marker portal (introduced by an Act 6 quest from 3.13.0); home of the fence Faustus, administrator Kurai, rogues and the Wayfinder Adiyah who opens contract portals.

nodes.name: The Ring
nodes.summary: Rogue guild that runs the Rogue Harbour and fulfils Heist contracts for clients such as Administrator Qotra and the Crimson Scribe. The Count Geonor passage in the wiki says he contracted the Ring. Its leader is referred to only as 'the Boss'.

nodes.name: Kurai
nodes.summary: Administrator of the Rogue Harbour; starts the introductory Rogue Harbour quest in Act 6 and hands out the first contract.

nodes.name: Adiyah, the Wayfinder
nodes.summary: Maraketh warrior and Wayfinder of the Rogue Harbour who opens Heist and Grand Heist portals for the exile. Her sister Nashta the Usurper tried to incite a civil war in the Maraketh; Adiyah and the exile stop her in the questline's final contract.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: "Open portal to the contract zone by interacting with Adiyah"

nodes.name: Faustus, the Fence
nodes.summary: Rogue Harbour fence who buys Heist targets in exchange for Rogue's Markers. The Kalguur page says Faustus, like Johan, has his sights set on Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Karst
nodes.summary: Lockpicking rogue in the Rogue Harbour; a Ring member (Kurai: 'assist member Karst') who aids the exile on the Trial Run contract and whose hire unlocks Huck.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: "Talk to Karst, the Lockpick, the rogue that aids you"
'The Ring' dialogue: 'assist member Karst on this job'

nodes.name: Tibbs
nodes.summary: Brute-force and demolition rogue hireable in the Rogue Harbour. Running a contract with him unlocks Tullina.

sources.locator: Lead; "To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs" (Tullina page)
Lead: "To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs, the Giant"

nodes.name: Isla
nodes.summary: Engineer rogue hireable for Heists; per the wiki she worked under Inquisitor Dominus ~20 years before the PoE1 campaign and designed The Unbreakable, the design of which was stolen by the Templar. Also operates the Recombinator and Kalguuran Map Devices in Kingsmarch.

sources.locator: Lead and Lore: "a skillset she acquired working under Inquisitor Dominus"

nodes.name: Huck
nodes.summary: Former soldier who joined the Ring after his discharge and hunts a lost friend, Enoch, who died in Templar research on augmentations. Hireable in Heists; unlocked by a Karst contract, and his contract unlocks Niles.

sources.locator: Lead; Personal Questline; "To unlock Huck, run a contract with Karst" (Niles page); "Took it out not long after joining the Ring"

nodes.name: Niles
nodes.summary: Former Templar interrogator, hireable rogue in the Rogue Harbour (Counter-thaumaturgy). Unlocked by a Huck contract; his contract unlocks Vinderi.

sources.locator: Lead and Lore: "He is the former interrogator of the Templar"; "To unlock Niles, run a contract with Huck")

nodes.name: Vinderi
nodes.summary: Demolition and trap-disarmament rogue (the Dismantler) whose unique ability duplicates Heist chest contents. Unlocked by a Niles contract; his contract unlocks Gianna.

sources.locator: Lead and Heist ability; "To unlock Vinderi, run a contract with Niles"

nodes.name: Gianna
nodes.summary: Deception rogue (the Master of Disguise). Backstory: she worked at the Theopolis Thespian Society in Oriath, and her early contracts involve Templar uniforms. Unlocked by a Vinderi contract.

sources.locator: Lead and Lore: Theopolis Thespian Society; "To unlock Gianna, run a contract with Vinderi"

nodes.name: Tullina
nodes.summary: Agility rogue (the Catburglar). Her heist target is Merveil's Wedding Dress, which the History page ties to the Oriath wedding of Daresso and Merveil. Unlocked by a Tibbs contract; her contract unlocks Nenet.

sources.locator: Lead: "To unlock Tullina, run a contract with Tibbs, the Giant"
'Daresso and Merveil' section: Merveil's wedding dress as a Heist target

nodes.name: Nenet
nodes.summary: Faridun rogue (the Scout) hireable for Perception jobs. Unlocked by a Tullina contract. Her questline was never released in-game: it would have had the exile seek the Book of Jamanra to prove the Jamanra existed.

sources.locator: Lead; "To unlock Nenet, run a contract with Tullina"; questline note
'Jamanra' section: 'Nenet, a Faridun, tasked the exile with finding the Book of Jamanra'

nodes.name: Faridun
nodes.summary: Desert people of Vastiri set against the Maraketh; featured in PoE2 as well.

nodes.name: Administrator Qotra
nodes.summary: Figure named on flavour text of replica uniques and as a Heist contract client; Kalandra says she 'meddles with forces she does not understand'. Item Qotra's Regulator (Ritual league) may refer to her.

nodes.name: The Crimson Scribe
nodes.summary: Society named as the client on Heist contracts targeting the Seal of Solaris, Seal of Lunaris, Ez Myrae Tome, Staff of the First Sin Eater and Golden Ibis; its targets indicate interest in the Winter of the World and the primeval civilization.

nodes.name: The Boss of the Ring
nodes.summary: The unnamed 'Boss' who leads the Ring, per Kurai's dialogue ('the Boss has no tolerance for guests who do not obey his rules'). Identity is not established in the wiki; any name is fan theory.

sources.locator: 'The Ring' dialogue: 'The Boss would like to offer you the opportunity'

nodes.name: Ritual (altar mechanic)
nodes.summary: Ritual Altars spawn wave encounters inside a ritual circle; defeating monsters earns Favour/Tribute to buy items. PoE1 Ritual league gives no narrative; Vaal Ritual Altars may summon Atziri's Apparition; later Wildwood lore ties 'ritual altars' to the King in the Mists; PoE2 adopts it in Forbidden Rites.

nodes.name: The King in the Mists
nodes.summary: Chief of the Nameless shadow creatures in the Viridian Wildwood and enemy of the Maji. Boss of Affliction (PoE1, 3.23) and, in PoE2 Act 1 (Freythorn), the cult 'king' guarding the final Ritual altar. In Legacy of the Maji, Aoife recalls being drawn to him, believing him one of the Maji of old.

sources.locator: Unique items: drops from the King in the Mists
Aoife dialogue about the King in the Mists

nodes.name: The Viridian Wildwood
nodes.summary: Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World, where time loops in seasons. Contested by the Nameless and the King in the Mists; Chaos believes the forest did not exist until the 3.23 timeline.

sources.locator: paragraph on the forest not existing until 3.23.0

nodes.name: Chaos
nodes.summary: Impulse, a godlike entity that sees all possibilities across timelines and delights in mortals bending chance; once worshipped by the Vaal; master of the Trialmaster; opposed to Order. Aware that the exiles exist in parallel timelines (dev statement).

sources.locator: Community Team post: 'Chaos does not know what you truly are...'

nodes.name: Order
nodes.summary: Impulse opposed to Chaos, representing dominion and control; Hinekora is its servant per wiki analysis; in one timeline Order overcame Chaos through Venarius's enslavement of humanity.

nodes.name: The Trialmaster
nodes.summary: Servant of Chaos who runs the Trials of Chaos. Introduced in PoE1's Ultimatum league and encountered in PoE2 Act 3 and the endgame Trialmaster arena.

chronology.relative: Captured in the Vaal era; active in PoE1 3.14+ and PoE2 Act 3

sources.locator: Lead: "the Trialmaster offers the Trials of Chaos"
Lead: "He will offer the Trials of Chaos ... as directed by his master, Chaos"
Lead: Chaos is the Trialmaster's master
Ixchel entry: captured infiltrating the Temple of Chaos, became the Trialmaster

nodes.name: Ixchel
nodes.summary: Vaal Order of the Djinn member ('Godstealer') who stole the sleeping body of Yaomac for the Order; captured while infiltrating the Temple of Chaos and became the Trialmaster.

nodes.name: Yaomac
nodes.summary: Ancient Vaal god with three serpentine heads, worshipped by Vaalish priests. Ixchel stole his sleeping body for the Order of the Djinn; the Trialmaster refers to Yaomac when the player wins five or more times.

nodes.name: Temple of Chaos
nodes.summary: Vaal temple near the outskirts of Utzaal where commoners could attempt the Trials of Chaos to become high priests; in PoE2 Act 3, off the Chimeral Wetlands.

sources.locator: paragraph on the Temple of Chaos

nodes.name: Trials of Chaos
nodes.summary: Escalating wave trials in which a Trialmaster-set modifier is added each round; the player banks or risks rewards. PoE1 Ultimatum league (3.14), core in 3.23; PoE2 Ascension Trial of Chaos (Act 3 Temple of Chaos, up to 10 trials).

nodes.name: The Last to Die
nodes.summary: Last of the Vaal High Priest bloodline bound by Chaos's pact to the Blood Crucible; appears from the Coast in Scourge, asking the exile to continue in her place; Kalandra says she 'wanders still, forever fleeing, forever burdened by guilt'.

nodes.name: Blood Crucible
nodes.summary: Device that lets the player shift into the Nightmare and corrupt items; per The Last to Die it represents a pact between Chaos and the bloodlines of Vaal High Priests, functioning only while the last bloodline lives.

nodes.name: The Nightmare (Scourge realm)
nodes.summary: Ruined, demon-infested alternate version of Wraeclast the exile shifts into in Scourge; monsters there become the new Beyond monsters. Not the same as the Vaal 'crimson nightmare' realm of Atziri.

nodes.name: Scourge monsters
nodes.summary: Blood-crazed demonic monsters of the Scourge Nightmare realm. After the league they became the core game's Beyond monsters, and currencies such as Tainted Blessing came from them.

nodes.name: K'Tash, the Hate Shepherd
nodes.summary: Scourge boss (K'tash, the Hate Shepherd) that can spawn in the Nightmare realm depending on the monsters present; the wiki gives stats but no individual lore.

nodes.name: Ghorr, the Grasping Maw
nodes.summary: Scourge boss that can spawn in the Nightmare realm depending on the monsters present; the wiki gives stats and no individual lore.

nodes.name: Beidat, Archangel of Death
nodes.summary: Scourge boss (Archangel of Death) that can spawn in the Nightmare realm depending on the monsters present; the wiki gives stats and no individual lore.

nodes.name: Archnemesis modifiers
nodes.summary: Itemised modifiers applied to petrified monsters to build custom rare boss fights. The wiki gives no narrative explanation.

nodes.name: Sentinels
nodes.summary: Sentinel drones of the Sentinel league (Stalker, Apex and Pandemonium types) that empower monsters. Sentinel Power Cores charge filaments; Recombinators are a separate item. The wiki gives no in-world narrator.

nodes.name: Kalandra
nodes.summary: Ancient being with an owl's body and human head, trapped in the Lake of Kalandra since the primordial era; she observes the world, scorns gods as 'thieves of virtue', and plans escape. Visited by the Order of the Djinn and the Clayshaper among others. Namesake of the Mirror of Kalandra.

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars in primordial Wraeclast where Kalandra is trapped. The league version was a mirror-realm assembled from a Mirrored Tablet and was not added to the core game.

sources.locator: League Mechanic and note on core game

nodes.name: Ancient Etchings (Kalandra)
nodes.summary: Series of Ancient Etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra herself, recounting her entrapment, scorn for gods (Etching V: a conversation with someone implied to be Sin), and the Order of the Djinn's failed rescue (Etching VI).

sources.locator: Ancient Etchings entry (found throughout the Lake)

nodes.name: Kalandra trapped in the Lake
nodes.summary: Kalandra entered the Lake out of curiosity in the primordial era and found herself unable to leave, forgetting each attempt.

sources.locator: Lore: Ancient Etchings; History of Wraeclast 'The Lake of Kalandra'

nodes.name: Evilandra
nodes.summary: Hostile 'evil' reflection of Kalandra (ArbiterWildEvil in game files). She rarely appears in the Lake and has her own tile dialogue.

nodes.name: Mirror of Kalandra
nodes.summary: One of the rarest and most valuable currency items in the game, named after Kalandra; the Path of Exile logo resembles it. Kalandra's Touch, a league item, was added to the core drop pool after the league.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper that guards dangerous artefacts and prevents calamities; selects one orphan from each culture. Members include Jun, Janus Perandus, Saresh, Ixchel, Dhunan, Sumei (investigated Kalandra's duplication of artefacts). Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.

nodes.name: Sumei
nodes.summary: Historical Maraketh Order of the Djinn 'Master Lorekeeper' who investigated artefact duplication caused by Kalandra's influence.

nodes.name: Middengard
nodes.summary: Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast, homeland of the Kalguur; ruled by a king named Cadigan; it cannot be directly visited in the games.

nodes.name: Aldur
nodes.summary: First King of Kalguur and first Runefather, inventor of runesmithing (Verisium runes capturing starlight); his Runefathers forged the Triskelion Flame after his death.

nodes.name: Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: Rune-forged Kalguuran relic honouring Aldur; made a symbol of royal authority under Cadigan I; carried on the first Wraeclast expedition to purify poisoned rain/fish and raise a starlight barrier; stolen by Olroth and later destroyed in the exile's fight with him.

nodes.name: Runefathers
nodes.summary: Aldur's chosen apprentices and artisans of runesmithing; forged the Triskelion Flame to reunite fractured Middengard.

nodes.name: King Cadigan the Third
nodes.summary: Kalguuran king who, after reading the Vaal Cataclysm as an 'Omen', commissioned the first expedition to Wraeclast with the Triskelion Flame and banned gems after the Azmeri panicked at the sight of one.

chronology.relative: Shortly after the Vaal Cataclysm (first Kalguuran expedition)

nodes.name: The King (Cadigan) of Kalguur
nodes.summary: Current infamous ruler of Kalguur, always named Cadigan; rumoured to use artifice to extend life and spy on subjects; Kalguuran NPCs avoid speaking of him. In PoE2 he orders Vaal artifacts brought to Kalguur.

nodes.name: Vaal artifacts sought by the King
nodes.summary: Unspecified Vaal artifacts that the Kalguuran King ordered brought back to Kalguur (most went missing en route).

nodes.name: First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Expedition commissioned by Cadigan III after the Vaal Cataclysm 'Omen'; led by Olroth (Knights of the Sun), Uhtred (Order of the Chalice), Vorana (Black Scythe) and Medved (Druids of the Broken Circle); poisoned journey; colonisation; trade with Karui and Azmeri; gem panic; eventual collapse.

chronology.relative: Thousands of years before PoE1; soon after the Vaal Cataclysm

nodes.name: Priesthood conspiracy (stabbing of Olroth)
nodes.summary: High Priest Uhtred, suspecting Olroth of fighting for the horrors in his sleep, had a dozen priests stab him (71 wounds); Vorana killed all twelve; Olroth was encased in glass and Uhtred fled to an ancient site of power.

nodes.name: Medved's challenge
nodes.summary: A two-axe horror leader (recognised by Vorana as her beloved Medved) killed 42 challengers in 42 days; Vorana ordered a retreat; two villages fell.

nodes.name: Loss of the Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: The starlight barrier vanished as Vorana tried to adjust it; the Flame's altar was empty and all harbour ships but one had been burned. Vorana branded Uhtred a traitor, and Olroth's glass case was found empty. Uhtred had fled to an ancient shrine.

nodes.name: Olroth
nodes.summary: Leader of the Knights of the Sun, called the Gallant and later the Grim. Recorded the Empty-Eyed Fiend's killing of a young woman, fought the Fiend with a gem, was stabbed by priests, and returned as the undying horror the exile fights as the Expedition league boss.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)

nodes.name: Medved
nodes.summary: Leader of the Druids of the Broken Circle who claimed to peer into the past. He pioneered culling a horror species, challenged the horrors' leader alone and vanished. He returns as a horror boss in PoE1 (Medved, Feller of Heroes).

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)

nodes.name: Vorana
nodes.summary: Black Scythe mercenary leader and Medved's beloved. She killed the twelve priests who stabbed Olroth, took gem-infused rites into her own flesh and left the walls. Returns as the boss Vorana, Last to Fall.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)

nodes.name: Uhtred
nodes.summary: High Priest of the Order of the Chalice who declared the Vaal gems unclean, admitted responsibility for the attack on Olroth, and fled to an ancient shrine. Returns as the PoE1 boss Uhtred, Covetous Traitor.

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)

nodes.name: Knights of the Sun
nodes.summary: Powerful Kalguuran warriors/enforcers directly under the King; led by Olroth; religious scrutiny by them drove some emigration.

nodes.name: Druids of the Broken Circle
nodes.summary: Kalguuran nature-mystic sect led by Medved, who could see the future by 'peering into the past'. Medved lost that sight the night Olroth set out alone with a gem.

nodes.name: Black Scythe
nodes.summary: Kalguuran mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana, responsible for the expedition's defence and offence. Their artifacts are the currency of the Expedition NPC Tujen.

nodes.name: Remembrancers
nodes.summary: Kalguuran scribes who documented the explorations; the Prime Remembrancer's logbooks tell the expedition's fall.

nodes.name: Order of the Chalice
nodes.summary: Kalguuran priesthood (Priests of the Chalice) that interpreted the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes; Uhtred was its High Priest.

nodes.name: Vorniculia / horrors
nodes.summary: Horror species that attacked Kalguuran outposts; Olroth's Knights culled the Vorniculia.

nodes.name: The Empty-Eyed Fiend
nodes.summary: Entity Olroth could not defeat with blade or flame, prompting him to use gems; the Kalguur page links it to The Elder (identification inferred).

nodes.name: Dannig

nodes.name: Rog

nodes.name: Tujen

nodes.name: Gwennen
nodes.summary: Kalguuran gambler and Expedition NPC who sells unidentified equipment and takes Broken Circle artifacts.

nodes.name: The Lost Expedition (quest)

The Clayshaper (Ahkeli) is named Honoured Founder of the Order, which the wiki says was founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper.
Per the Oshabi page, after the tutorial quest Oshabi turns into the Heart of the Grove and is no longer available to talk to.

sources.locator: Lead: "After the tutorial quest, Oshabi will turn into the Heart of the Grove"

edges.description: Harvesting a Tier 4 seed grows the Heart of the Grove (about 100 cycles); once it finishes growing it can be harvested to challenge the Avatar of the Grove.

sources.locator: League mechanic: "Harvesting a Tier 4 seed will cause a Heart of the Grove to grow" ... "challenge the Avatar of the Grove"

edges.description: Adiyah's sister Nashta, the Usurper.
Nashta is a Maraketh warrior who tried to incite civil war within the Maraketh.

sources.locator: Lore: "Nashta ... tried to incite a civil war within the Maraketh"

edges.description: In the final Heist contract (Heart of Glory) the exile and Adiyah confront and kill Nashta.

sources.locator: Lore: "Adiyah and the player then kill her"

edges.description: The Order of the Djinn was founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper.

sources.locator: Lead: "It was founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper."
